Sec. 3 'Previous linguistic research' names Capo's comparative Gbe work and SIL word lists; informants report 'minor differences in tone and pronunciation' between villages. Reference list includes Hazoumê 1981 'Une esquisse phonologique du tofingbe' (CNL Cotonou).

sources.citation: Gbéto, Flavien. 2004. Tonologie synchronique du tɔfingbe du village lacustre de Ganvié, dialecte gbe du Sud-Bénin. Journal of West African Languages 31(2): 27-46.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. A tonology of the Ganvié variety: two underlying tones H and B (non-H), surface M and BH derived by consonant-conditioned lowering/spreading rules; sections on consonants, syllable structure, tone distribution in nouns/verbs. 'accent' appears only as names of tone diacritics (fn. 2, p. 28); no statement on word stress or accent.
Infobox 'langue à tons'; no stress statement; bibliography lists Gbéto 2004 and Hazoumè's esquisse phonologique.
